text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Nigerian security agents arrest and detain former oil minister Don Etiebet, leader of one of five registered political parties, for undisclosed reasons.

- Government may opt for restructuring rather than liquidating three distressed banks -- ICON Merchant Bank, Continental Merchant Bank and Nigerian Merchant Bank, paper says, citing own investigation.
- Southwestern Ondo state to soon commission a modern wood processing plant at a cost of 264 million naira in the capital city Akure, military administrator Navy Captain Anthony Onyearugbulem says.
- Four killed and several others injured in southern Delta and Rivers states as violence erupts after last Saturday's local council polls.

- Jani Ibrahim, new manager of ailing national carrier Nigerian Airways, says the airline will soon resume flying the Lagos-London route. British aviation authorities barred the carrier from landing at London's Heathrow airport because it had no valid insurance cover for its planes.

- Telecommunications sector regulator Nigerian Communications Commission gives licences to 23 new private companies to provide and operate different services in the country. A total of 61 companies have now received such licences.
- Radical lawyer and human rights activist Gani Fawehinmi alleges that unknown persons plan to assassinate him.

- Special vessel ordered by Nigerian subsidiary of Chevron Corp for lifting liquefied petroluem gas (LPG) to overseas markets from midwestern Escravos gas project site arrives. May 1 is start-up date of project.

- Sam Aluko, chairman of government agency National Economic Intelligence Committee (NEIC), says last week's devaluation of the naira at the autonomous foreign exchange market to 85 naira from 80 naira was nothing to worry about.
